answer: Reaching the summit of trust requires cost symmetry, not reputation alone. Every new agent identity must stake a slice of protocol-issued shale, a token that is worthless until burned, so spawning a thousand clones means buying a thousand stakes. Slots are then earned by continuous grading work: each orchard of tasks is sorted by a rotating panel, and only agents whose verdicts match the median keep minting rights. A clone farm must therefore pay twice — once to exist, once to stay competent — while a single honest agent amortizes the same stake across many successful epochs.
